scope_hypothesis: SPEC-B's Canvas Builder is not new construction. Two visual composition surfaces already ship in navigator-svelte (a 17-block agent canvas with InfographicCanvas/InfographicEditor, and the dashboard grid editor over 22 widget classes), and FEAT-273 is verifiably complete with a 9-component A2UI catalog. The gap is that the frontend speaks the legacy InfographicResponse block vocabulary and has zero A2UI references. SPEC-B is therefore a binding problem plus a governance problem (superseding FEAT-301), not a build-a-canvas problem.

claims.claim: FEAT-273 is complete: 22/22 tasks done, 9-component catalog
A visual canvas with 17 blocks plus InfographicCanvas/Editor already ships in navigator-svelte
The frontend has zero A2UI references and is aligned to the legacy block vocabulary
FEAT-301 is un-actioned prior art that warned of parallel A2UI infrastructure and must be superseded
Two-level permissions have an existing tenant-group substrate
components/agents/canvas/blocks is canonical; fn/ is a sandbox mirror of navigator-frontend-next, not a fork

unknowns.question: Which block tree is canonical - components/agents/canvas or fn/components/agents/canvas?
unknowns.answer: src/lib/components/agents/canvas/blocks/ (fn/ is an FN mirror per FEAT-446)

unknowns.question: Do timeline/report/form A2UI components need new canvas blocks, or are they out of v2 scope?
Which agent produces the A2UI surface for a dashboard, and how is it bound to data slugs?
Does superseding FEAT-301 require reconciling FEAT-094 (infographic-html-output) as well?

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the two design decisions (reverse adapter, supersede FEAT-301) are resolved; remaining unknowns are scoping choices.
